'''Bengt Ingemar Samuelsson''' (21 May 1934 – 5 July 2024) was a Swedish [[biochemist]]. He shared with [[Sune K. Bergström]] and [[John R. Vane]] the 1982 [[Nobel Prize]] for Physiology or Medicine for discoveries concerning [[prostaglandin]]s and related substances.<ref>{{Citation
|pmid = 10584758
|last=Raju
|first=T N
|publication-date= 27 November 1999
|year=1999
|title=The Nobel chronicles. 1982: Sune Karl Bergström (b 1916); Bengt Ingemar Samuelsson (b 1934); John Robert Vane (b 1927)
|volume=354
|issue=9193
|periodical=[[The Lancet|Lancet]]
|pages=1914
|doi=10.1016/s0140-6736(05)76884-7
|s2cid=54236400
}}</ref><ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20091026062757/http://www.geocities.com/med_1980kkk/samuelsson-autobio.html|title=Swedish Medical Association's Jubilee Award}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Samuelsson was born in [[Halmstad]] in southwest Sweden, studied at [[Lund University]], and was a professor in medical and physiological chemistry at [[Karolinska Institute]] in Stockholm in 1973. He was president of [[Karolinska Institute]] from 1983 to 1995 and chairman of the [[Nobel Foundation]] from 1993 to 2005.<ref name="nobel-bio" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Bent I. Samuelson - Biographical |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/1982/samuelsson/biographical/ |access-date=2 December 2025 |website=nobelprize.org}}</ref>

==Research and career==
Discussing the role of [[prostaglandin]]s in the body, Samuelsson explained, "It's a control system for the cells that participates in many biological functions. There are endless possibilities of manipulating this system in drug development."

His research interests were originally in [[cholesterol]] metabolism with importance to reaction mechanisms. Following the structural work on prostaglandins along with Sune Bergström he was interested mainly in the transformation products of [[arachidonic acid]]. This has led to the identification of [[endoperoxide]]s, [[thromboxane]]s and the [[leukotriene]]s, and his group has chiefly been involved in studying the [[chemistry]], [[biochemistry]] and [[biology]] of these compounds and their function in biological control systems. This research has implications in numerous clinical areas, especially in [[thrombosis]], [[inflammation]], and [[allergy]].<ref name="nobel-bio">{{cite web |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/1982/samuelsson/biographical/ |title=Bengt I. Samuelsson – Biographical |publisher=Nobel Foundation |access-date=1 March 2026}}</ref><ref name="nobel-press">{{cite web |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/1982/press-release/ |title=The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1982 – Press release |publisher=Nobel Foundation |access-date=1 March 2026}}</ref><ref name="mayo">{{cite journal |last1=Shampo |first1=M. A. |last2=Kyle |first2=R. A. |title=Bengt Samuelsson—Nobel Prize Winner for Studies of Prostaglandins, Thromboxanes, and Leukotrienes |journal=Mayo Clinic Proceedings |date=December 1997 |volume=72 |issue=12 |page=1158 |doi=10.1016/S0025-6196(11)63681-1 |pmid=9413298}}</ref>

This field has grown enormously since those days. Between 1981 and 1995, about 3,000 papers per year were published that specifically used the expression "prostaglandins," or related terms such as "prostacyclins," "leukotrienes," and "thromboxanes," in their labels and titles.<ref name="raju">{{cite journal |last=Raju |first=T. N. |title=The Nobel chronicles. 1982: Sune Karl Bergström (b 1916); Bengt Ingemar Samuelsson (b 1934); John Robert Vane (b 1927) |journal=The Lancet |date=27 November 1999 |volume=354 |issue=9193 |page=1914 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(05)76884-7 |pmid=10584758 |s2cid=54236400}}</ref>

Samuelsson had served as a director on the boards of [[Pharmacia]] AB, [[NicOx]] SA, and [[Bayer Schering Pharma AG|Schering]] AG, and was an advisor to the venture capital fund [[HealthCap]].<ref name="healthcap">{{cite web |url=https://www.healthcap.eu/media/healthcap-senior-advisor-bengt-samuelsson-has-passed-away-at-the-age-of-90/ |title=HealthCap senior advisor Bengt Samuelsson has passed away at the age of 90 |publisher=HealthCap |date=2024 |access-date=1 March 2026}}</ref><ref name="nicox">{{cite web |url=https://www.nicox.com/election-of-vicente-anido-jr-to-nicoxs-board-of-directors-vaughn-kailian-re-elected-director/ |title=Election of Vicente Anido, Jr. to Nicox's Board of Directors – Vaughn Kailian re-elected Director |publisher=Nicox |date=20 June 2013 |access-date=1 March 2026}}</ref><ref name="ki-obit">{{cite web |url=https://news.ki.se/nobel-laureate-and-former-ki-president-bengt-samuelsson-has-passed-away |title=Nobel laureate and former KI president, Bengt Samuelsson, has passed away |publisher=Karolinska Institutet |date=15 July 2024 |access-date=1 March 2026}}</ref>

==Death==
Samuelsson died on 5 July 2024, at the age of 90.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dn.se/familj/dodsannonser/#/CaseInline/914436 | title=Dödsannonser - DN.se }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=7 July 2024 |title=Svenske Nobelpristagaren Bengt Samuelsson död |url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/a/4Bo81e |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=www.aftonbladet.se |language=sv}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1982 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/1982/samuelsson/facts/ |access-date=8 July 2024 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US |archive-date=5 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240405024650/https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/1982/samuelsson/facts/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
In 1975, Samuelsson was awarded the [[Louisa Gross Horwitz Prize]] from [[Columbia University]] together with [[Sune K. Bergström]]. He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1990|Foreign Member of the Royal Society (ForMemRS) in 1990]].<ref name=formemrs/>
